transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE), Connor Blake (Redwood SE) -- Maya Thompson (Lynx CTO), Jordan Ellis (Lead Eng), Priya Nair (Security), Aaron Lee (Product)

Summary (auto): align on POC goals, sizing, benchmarks, integration pattern for OpenAI-compatible endpoints and function calling; agree next steps to run benchmarks and share security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood Inference, this is Elena and Connor on the technical side. Maya, Jordan, Priya, Aaron, thanks for your time. Want to run through goals, success criteria, and integration details.
[00:12] Maya: Hi Samir, thanks. High level: we want to validate integration into our orchestration layer, ensure latency under 250ms p95 for short chat prompts, and ensure cost per interaction is within our target. Also want to test function/tool calling for our agent flows.
[00:28] Jordan: Yep, and just to add, our traffic profile is spiky — mid-day bursts up to 600 qps for small prompts, longer generation requests around 50 qps. We want to understand batching behavior and how Redwood handles KV cache for context.
[00:47] Elena: cool. A couple clarifying q's: when you say 250ms p95 is that end-to-end from your app into the endpoint or just model generation time?
[00:56] Maya: end-to-end including network hop from our EU region into the endpoint. We're open to dedicated if it helps hit SLOs but want cost comparatives.
[01:07] Connor: noted. We'll recommend both a hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint test (fast to iterate) and a Dedicated run for throughput/latency benchmarks, same model family. We do a KV cache/prefix cache test to simulate persona-handoff.
[01:22] Jordan: On the integration side we need SDK parity — our stack uses the OpenAI SDK today. Can Redwood expose an OpenAI-compatible REST endpoint and drop-in SDK support?
[01:32] Samir: yes that's a common ask. We provide OpenAI-compatible endpoints plus official SDKs (JS, Python, Go). You can use the same client calls; function calling and streaming are supported. Note sometimes the verbatim protocol has tiny differences—we'll send the compatibility doc.
[01:48] Aaron: any differences for tool/function calling plumbing? We use structured JSON responses and then route to internal tools.
[01:55] Elena: Redwood supports function/tool calling semantics similar to OpenAI's — you can surface tools, get structured JSON, and also use our structured output templates to validate schemas at generation time. There are rate-limit considerations when you call external tools from within the same transaction, so we'll show patterns.
[02:12] Priya: security question: we need SOC 2 type II, customer-managed KMS, and VPC peering for Private deployment. How mature are those?
[02:21] Samir: Redwood has SOC 2, and Dedicated/Private support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and VPC options. For POC we'll probably start hosted in a region with encryption at rest, then do a Private/Dedicated validation if you need peering. We'll share the security pack.
[02:36] Maya: timeline wise we want a 4-week POC: week 1 integration + sanity tests, week 2 bench runs, week 3 quality checks and tuning, week 4 decision and exec review. Feels tight but doable.
[02:49] Samir: sounds good. For benchmarks we'll need: sample prompt set, 99/95/50 latency targets, target throughput and concurrency, and a cost target per 1k tokens or per interaction.
[03:02] Jordan: we'll provide the prompts and expected TP/latency. One more, we need to validate structured output determinism — e.g., strict JSON schema enforcement and reranking accuracy. How do we measure quality regressions?
[03:14] Connor: we recommend a holdout eval set and automated quality metrics (exact match, schema validation, hallucination checks). Redwood Optimize can run differential evals across model versions; during POC we can instrument that.
[03:27] Aaron: and for workload sizing, what's your recommended test config to simulate spikes?
[03:32] Elena: typically we run two phases: steady-state ramp to expected qps (e.g., 100 qps) and spike tests to 2x-3x for short windows. We also test long-context behavior with larger sequence lengths to check memory/KV impacts.
[03:47] Maya: ok. On the integration side, our timeline for engineering is week of Dec 7 to start heavy lift. Is that compatible?
[03:55] Samir: yes, we can align. We'll provision a short-lived Dedicated reservation or sandbox hosted endpoint depending on your preference. For immediate testing, an OpenAI-compatible hosted endpoint will remove friction.
[04:07] Jordan: about tokens and cost — do you have tooling to estimate per-call cost with batching and cache?
[04:13] Connor: yes our Console provides token-level cost breakdowns and we can run cost simulations given your prompt corpus. Batching profiles depend on concurrency and latency targets; we'll provide suggested batch sizes.
[04:25] Priya: can you confirm log retention and access controls? We need audit logs for any PII, and the ability to disable retention for specific routes.
[04:32] Elena: audit logs are supported; you can set retention per-route in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we have options to disable retention for customer routes used in PII flows during POC. We'll include the doc.
[04:45] Maya: any caveats when using function calling with streaming? We want tokens as they arrive to start downstream processing.
[04:52] Connor: streaming + function calling is supported. There are two patterns: stream events + final function call payload, or stream partial function args depending on your toolchain. We'll propose the approach that minimizes reassembly on your side.
[05:05] Samir: for benchmarks we'll propose using our benchmarking harness (we'll send a link) that runs openai-compatible calls and measures p50/p95/p99 as well as cost. We'll also run KV cache hit-rate scenarios.
[05:18] Jordan: good. For the POC success criteria, we propose: 1) end-to-end p95 < 250ms for short prompts, 2) maintain quality parity (>=95% on schema validation for structured outputs), 3) cost within 20% of our target, 4) security checklist satisfied for Private/Dedicated.
[05:34] Samir: that's a solid set. We'll map each to an acceptance test. We'll also propose fallback policies for overloaded windows — model variant routing, and throughput throttling.
[05:46] Maya: one practical—our orchestration calls the API with a tool manifest that includes multiple tool signatures. How do you surface tool metadata on the endpoint?
[05:55] Elena: we support tool manifests and the ability to register tool schemas; tool discovery metadata can be passed to the model via the OpenAI-compatible function calling fields. We'll share example manifest format.
[06:07] Aaron: do you have example SDK snippets for TypeScript showing function calling and structured output enforcement?
[06:12] Samir: yes, will include in the follow-up package — SDK snippets, a mini-integration guide, and a sample app.
[06:20] Jordan: any known limitations with long context windows and quantized models we should be aware of?
[06:26] Connor: quantization can slightly affect long-context numeric stability in some cases; for the POC we'll test both fp16 and quantized variants to measure QoE. The runtime has optimizations for attention and KV cache to keep latency predictable.
[06:40] Priya: if we decide to do Private deployment after POC, how long to stand up?
[06:45] Samir: typical Private onboarding is 6-8 weeks for peering, KMS integration, and compliance checks, but we can parallelize some security work during the POC.
[06:56] Maya: excellent. Let's confirm the benchmark schedule: provide prompts by 12/3, Redwood provisions test endpoints by 12/4, bench run 12/7-12/9, results and tuning 12/10-12/14, decision 12/17.
[07:10] Samir: noted. We'll send the benchmark template later today and aim to provision the sandbox early next week.
[07:18] Aaron: any enterprise procurement items we should prepare? Contract, IP, data handling?
[07:24] Samir: we'll include a starter SOW and the security pack; procurement items usually include DPA, SLA addendum, and ordering info.
[07:33] Maya: ok thanks. Anything else?
[07:36] Elena: just to reiterate, please include sample SDK calls for streaming function calling and a sample manifest for structured output.
[07:44] Connor: and we'll include the benchmark harness link + instructions to run locally or via Redwood-managed runner.
[07:50] Samir: great. Recap and next steps: Samir sends benchmark template, pricing, SOW draft, SDK snippets, and security pack. Elena provisions sandbox. Lynx provides prompt corpus and security requirements. We'll schedule the bench run week of Dec 7.
[08:06] Maya: perfect — thanks everyone.
[08:08] Samir: thanks, we'll follow up via email and update CRM.

End of transcript.
